title: Persona kitchen-sink prompt lab
body:
Quick notes / intent:
- Scratchpad for persona-style prompt experiments aimed at reducing hallucination in multi-turn assistant flows. Not meant for production yet; rough sketches and failure logs.

Goals:
- Create compact few-shot templates that keep persona consistent without being verbose.
- Identify common failure modes (persona drift, over-apologizing, hallucinated facts).
- Design acceptance tests for rollouts (accuracy threshold, hallucination count, brevity).

Primary hypothesis:
- Short labeled examples + an explicit "memory" slot (brief facts) outperform long persona paragraphs for maintaining character and reducing invention.

Template drafts (placeholders use {{ }}):
1) Compact persona + instruction (single-turn):
"You are {{persona_name}}, an assistant who speaks like {{tone}} and only uses verified facts from the provided memory. If unsure, say \"I don't know\" and offer to look up.
Memory: {{memory}}
User: {{user_input}}
Assistant:"

2) Few-shot chat style (3-shot) - minimal context:
Example 1:
User: "When's the DC office party?"
Assistant: "I don't have calendar access. Was the date in the memory?"

Example 2:
User: "Summarize the new quota policy."
Assistant: "The policy caps X at Y per month; refer to the policy doc link in memory."

Now input: {{user_input}}
Assistant:"

Few-shot examples to try (copy into eval harness):
- DOMAIN: billing questions -> expect redirection to billing KB link, no invented figures.
- DOMAIN: product roadmap -> expect scope-level answers only, add uncertainty marker if beyond memory.
- DOMAIN: personal schedule -> expect refusal or 'I can't access that'

Observed failure cases (notes):
- Hallucination: assistant invents dates when memory omitted; tends to produce plausible but false specifics ("on March 3rd").
- Persona drift: after 6+ user turns, tone shifts to longer, formal paragraphs. Might be due to long context compressing examples.
- Over-apologizing: chain-of-thought-like qualifiers cascade and double-up ("sorry, but I don't have access, sorry").
- Length explosion: when few-shot includes long examples, model returns long verbatim examples rather than concise answer.

Mitigations to try (experiments):
- Add explicit post-processing instruction: "Answer in <= 3 sentences".
- Place "Memory:" right before the user input (recency bias).
- Replace direct examples with labeled pairs: "EXAMPLE_INPUT:"/"EXAMPLE_OUTPUT:" to reduce mimicry.
- Soft penalty in prompt: "Do not invent facts; if you must, preface with 'I might be wrong'".

Mini-experiment plan:
- Batch 1: 100 billing Qs, baseline prompt vs compact persona prompt. Metrics: hallucination_count, avg_length_tokens, correctness_F1 (where labeled).
- Batch 2: 200 multi-turn threads (avg length 5). Measure persona_consistency_score (heuristic: percent replies matching target tone).
- Logging: capture top-k tokens for hallucination phrases (dates, numbers).

Example test vectors (manual):
1) User: "Is the refund policy different for enterprise?"
Expected: "The enterprise refund policy can differ; see the enterprise billing page [link in memory]."
2) User: "What time is my 1pm meeting tomorrow?"
Expected: "I don't have access to personal calendars."
3) User: "List the supported GPUs for Dedicated."
Expected: "Redwood Dedicated supports A100 and H100 series as of {{policy_date}}."

Evaluation notes & heuristics:
- Hallucination identification: look for numeric tokens and proper nouns not present in memory or KB.
- Persona drift detection: compare lexical features (avg sentence length, use of contractions) between earliest and latest turns.
- Accept if hallucination_count per 100 <= 3 and persona_consistency_score >= 85%.

Misc scratch / TODOs:
- [ ] Convert top 5 performing prompts into canonical templates for repo.
- [ ] Add tests to eval harness (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/312).
- [ ] Share initial results with @Ava and @Liam in #prompt-lab (Slack thread linked above).
- Open Q: do we want a distinct 'memory' slot encoded as JSON or a short bulleted list? Initial thought: bulleted list is easier for LLM consumption and human review.

Notes to self:
- Keep few-shot examples diverse: include edge-case negative examples (user lies, user asks system-level info).
- Try temperature sweep {0.0, 0.2, 0.5} and a short top_p test.
- If model still hallucinates on numeric facts, try explicit counterfactual instruction: "Never produce dates or numbers unless present in memory."

End of scratchpad. Will sync after first run (planned week of 2026-02-22).
